WORKSHEETS APPENDIX D: EXAMPLE MSDS’S Page7 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version 1 EXECUTIVE SUMMARY This report presents the findings of a year-long pre-FEED study into the feasibility of a CO intermodal hub 2 in Port Tampa Bay which would collect, store, and liquify captured CO from major emitters across the 2 State of Florida for marine transport out of the state. The proposed hub is called the Tampa Regional Intermodal Carbon Hub (T-RICH). The study was funded by the National Energy Technology Laboratory (NETL) of the U.S. Department of Energy under Award No. DE-FE0032464. The study was completed on time and under budget. The main objective of the project was to determine if it would be technically feasible to build an intermodal CO hub on an available parcel of land in Port Tampa Bay for export to Class VI sequestration 2 wells or for enhanced oil recovery in Louisiana or Texas on specialized liquified CO carrying ships. The 2 secondary objective was to determine the cost of building such a hub to determine if it is economically and commercially viable. The goal for hub throughput was initially set at 2 million tons per annum (mtpa). For reference, the average individual CO emissions of electricity generating plants within 30 miles of the 2 hub are between 2 and 3 mtpa, and the combined emissions from the Greater Tampa region exceed 30 mtpa. The principal findings of the study are: 1. A 2mtpa CO hub will require approximately 8.5 acres of land area. This is a little more than half 2 of the available parcel of land chosen for the study in Port Tampa Bay. There are several other available parcels in the port that may also be suitable. 2. With a total area of almost 16 acres, the chosen parcel could be expanded upon to achieve a total throughput of 8 mtpa, or four times the initial throughput goal. 3.
